(Exparte)
 Judgment
The petitioner has filed this petition U/Sec.166 of the Motor Vehicles Act claiming compensation for the injuries sustained by him in a road traffic accident that occurred on 12.12.2022.

Chunchegowda vs N.E.K.S.R.T.C on 10 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/178061914/
1 2.

The petition averments in brief are as under:
On 12.12.2022 at about 6.30 to 6.35 a.m., the petitioner was proceeding as a pillion rider of motor cycle bearing No. KA-11-ET-1709 towards Pandavapura railway station and when he reached near Pandavapura railway station circle, Pandavapura-Mysore road, Mandya, at that time the driver of KEKSRTC bus bearing No. KA-36-F-1473 drove the same in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against the motor cycle.
Due to the said impact, the petitioner sustained grievous injuries.

Immediately after the accident, he was shifted to Govt. hospital, Pandavapura wherein he took first aid treatment and later he was shifted to KR Hospital, Mysore and later shifted to Prajwal Health Care Nagarajegowda Memorial Hospital, wherein he was admitted as inpatient and he has spent Rs.50,000/- towards hospitalization charges, treatment medicines, conveyance, nourishing food and other incidental charges etc.,

entities.text: Prajwal Health Care Nagarajegowda Memorial Hospital
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: Prior to the accident, petitioner was very hale and healthy and he was working as coolie and earning Rs.25,000/- p.m.
Due to the accidental injuries petitioner is not able to continue his work and is under complete bed rest and he is suffering from permanent disability.
The respondent No.1 is the owner and internal insurer of the bus and respondent No.2 is the driver of the bus are liable to pay compensation of Rs.10,00,000/- with interest.
3. After service of notices respondent No.1 appeared through its counsel and filed written statement.
Respondent No.2 remained absent hence, placed exparte.
The respondent No.1 filed written statement by denying that the accident was occurred due to negligence on the part of driver of BMTC bus bearing No. KA-36-F- 1473.
Further contended that the accident was occurred due to over speed and rash and negligent riding of the motor cycle bearing No. KA-11-ET-1709 in which the petitioner was proceeding.

Further denied the age,
avocation, alleged disability and income of the petitioner.
The compensation claimed by the petitioner is highly excessive and exorbitant.
Hence, the respondent No.1 prays to dismiss the petition against it.

4. On the basis of the rival contention, the following issues are framed by this court:
1.

Whether the petitioner proves that he has sustained grievous injuries due to the actionable negligent driving of NEKSRTC bus bearing Reg. No. KA-36- F-1473 by its driver, in RTA took place on 12.12.2022 at about 6.30 to 6.35 a.m. near Pandavapura railway station circle, Pandavapura Railway station, Mandya?
2. Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation?

If so, at what rate and from whom?
Chunchegowda vs N.E.K.S.R.T.C on 10 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/178061914/
2

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
3. What Order or Award?
5.
In order to prove the claim petition, the petitioner examined himself as P.W.1 and got marked the documents at Ex.P.1 to 11.
Dr. B. Ramesh, Orthopaedic Surgeon at Victoria Hospital is examined as PW.2, through him got marked Ex.P12 & 13.
The driver of the bus is examined as RW.1 and two documents Ex.R1 & 2 are marked.

6. Heard the arguments of both sides and perused the material evidence that are available on record.
7.
My findings on the above issues are as under.

Issue No.1 : In the affirmative;
 Issue No.2 : Partly in the affirmative  Issue No.3 : As per final orders

for the following:-
 : R E A S O N S:
 ISSUE NO.1 :
8.
That by reiterating all the averments made in the petition, the petitioner has filed his affidavit in lieu of- examination in-chief, which is considered as P.W.1.

In support of his case, he has produced true copies of FIR, complaint, statement witness, mahazar, charge sheet and IMV report, which are marked under Ex.P.1 to 6.
9.

On perusal of Ex.P1, FIR is registered on the basis of the Ex.P2 first information which is given by the relative of petitioner by alleging the negligence act of the driver of bus bearing No.
KA-36-F-1473.

The contents of Ex.P2 complaint and Ex.P1 FIR supports the contention of the petitioner against the negligence driving of the driver of bus bearing No. KA-36-F-1473 which is owned and insured by the respondent No.1.
In continuation of Ex.P1 & 2, the police drawn spot mahazar which is marked as Ex.P4.
At the time of Ex.P4, the rough sketch is also drawn by the police.

It is very important to note that in the written statement of the respondent, the respondent admitted the incident but denied the part of negligence by the driver of bus bearing No. KA-36-F- 1473.
10.

On perusal of Ex.P4 mahazar and rough sketch appended the accident is occurred in the right side of the road wherein the driver of bus bearing No. KA-36-F-1473 came to his right side and dashed against the bike in which the petitioner was proceeding.
The Ex.P6 IMV report depicts that the front bumper of the bus bearing No. KA-36-F-1473 has got damaged and front left side of the bike bearing No. KA-11-ET- 1709 has got damaged.
Thus, the contents of Ex.P4 mahazar and rough sketch and ExP.6 IMV report prima-facie establishes the negligence on the part of driver of bus bearing No. KA-36-F-1473.

Chunchegowda vs N.E.K.S.R.T.C on 10 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/178061914/
3 11.
The driver of bus bearing No. KA-36-F-1473 examined himself as RW.1 and deposed by denying the rash and negligent driving.
But failed to disbelieve the contents of Ex.P4 mahazar.
The driver of bus bearing No. KA-36-F-1473 came to his right side and dashed against the bike in which the petitioner was coming from opposite direction.
Thus, as the accident is head on collusion the reason for the alleged accident is the bus which came to its right side direction.

entities.text:
2009 ACJ 287 ( National Ins. Co. V/s.
Pushparama and others)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Proceedings under Motor Vehicles Act are not akin to proceedings in a Civil Court.
Hence, strict rules of evidence are not required to be followed in this regard.

12. Hence, by relying on the said precedent and in the absence of rebuttal evidence and denial in respect of police documents marked at Ex.P1 to 7 & 9, this court is of the opinion that the accident has happened due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of bus bearing No. KA-36-F-1473.
13.

In a claim for compensation under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, the claimant is to prove the incident only on preponderance of probabilities and the standard of proof beyond reasonable doubt is not required as held by Hon'ble Supreme Court in the decision reported in 2011 SAR (CIVIL) 319 Kusum and others V/s Satbir and others.

entities.text: 2011 SAR (CIVIL) 319 Kusum and others V/s Satbir and others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 14. Further the Hon'ble Supreme Court in case of Bimla Devi and others v. Himachal Road Transport Corporation and others (2009) 13 SCC 530, wherein it is held that, it was necessary to be borne in mind that strict proof of an accident caused by a particular bus in a particular manner may not be possible to be done by the claimants.

entities.text: Bimla Devi and others v. Himachal Road Transport Corporation and others (2009) 13 SCC 530
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The claimants were merely to establish their case on the touchstone of preponderance of probability.
The standard of proof beyond reasonable doubt could not have been applied.

15. In support of these documentary evidence, if we perused the oral evidence of the petitioner on this point, even though the respondent cross-examined the petitioner, nothing been elicited to disbelieve the case of the petitioner.
The respondent being the owner has not stated any grounds which caused the injuries to the petitioner except denying the case of the petitioner.

16. In this context by considering the contents of Ex.P1 to 7 & 9 this court tilts in favour of the petitioner as the petitioner has to prove the alleged negligence on the basis of the evidence and proof of the same on preponderance of probabilities.

The Ex.P 5 charge sheet also supports the view of this court, as the charge sheet filed for the offence punishable under Sec. 279, 337 & 338 of IPC against the driver of bus bearing No. KA-36-F- 1473.

Chunchegowda vs N.E.K.S.R.T.C on 10 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/178061914/
4 17.
As per well settled principle of law, the standard of proof in the claim petition like the present is preponderance of the probability.
There are no grounds to disbelieve the case of petitioner in the absence of rebuttal evidence.

All the materials available on record leading to show that, petitioner has sustained injuries in the accident took place on 12.12.2022 which is caused by the driver of the the driver of bus bearing No. KA-36- F-1473 which belonging to respondent No.1.
There is no reasons to discard the evidence of petitioner.
In the claim petition like present one strict proof is not necessary but preponderance of probabilities is sufficient.
Accordingly, I answer issue No.1 in the affirmative.

ISSUE NO.2:
18.
As already held herein above, the petitioner has proved that he has sustained injuries in RTA which is caused by the driver of NEKSRTC bus bearing No. KA- 36-F-1473 belongs to respondent No.1.
Hence, the petitioner is entitle for compensation.
Now the quantum of compensation is to be ascertained on different heads.
a) PAIN AND AGONY :-
At the time of alleged accident the petitioner was aged about 62 years.
The petitioner has produced Aadhaar card at Ex.P8 the year of birth of the petitioner as 1948 hence, as on the date of accident, the petitioner was aged about 74 years at the time of accident.

In the petition itself he has averred that immediately after the accident he was admitted to Govt.
Hospital and after first aid he was shifted to KR Hospital, Mysore and later shifted to Prajwal Health Care Nagarajegowda Memorial Hospital, wherein he was admitted as inpatient from on 13.12.2022 and discharged on 16.12.2022.

entities.text: Prajwal Health Care Nagarajegowda Memorial Hospital
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: As per the discharge summary marked at Ex.P10 the petitioner sustained left undisplaced fracture calcaneus.
He took conservative treatment.
If we perused the evidence of the doctor certainly the injuries mentioned in the wound certificate is causing a considerable disability to the petitioner.
No other evidence is placed by the respondent to disbelieve the evidence of the doctor in this regard.
By considering the nature of the injuries and period he spent to overcome the pain and other allied effects of the accident Rs.25,000/- may be awarded to the petitioner under this head.
b) Medical expenses:
The petitioner has produced 11 medical bills as per Ex.P11, amounting to Rs.23,169/-.
These documents are not disproved by the respondents, except mere denial and there is also no reasons to disbelieve the medical bills.
Hence the petitioner is entitle for medical expenses.
The said amount is rounded off to Rs.24,000/-.
c) Loss of income during laid up period:
The petitioner has stated that he was working as coolie and earning Rs.25,000/- p.m.
To prove the said fact the petitioner has not produced any document.
To consider the avocation of the petitioner except the oral evidence, no documents or proof of salary is shown by the petitioner.
Such being the case it is just and necessary to consider the notional income of the petitioner at Rs.15,500/- p.m. as the accident is of the year 2022.

Chunchegowda vs N.E.K.S.R.T.C on 10 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/178061914/
5
As per the discharge summary marked at Ex.P10- the petitioner was admitted to Nagarajegowda Memorial Hospital on 13.12.2022 and discharged on 16.12.2022 for 4 days.

Thereafter usually the healing period has to be considered for which in the absence of evidence this court is of the opinion that in total two months may be considered under this head as a loss of income.
So, the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.15,500 X 2= Rs.31,000/- during the laid up period.

d) Disability;- To prove the nature of injuries sustained by him the petitioner examined Dr.B.
Ramesh, Orthopedic Surgeon at Victoria Hospital is examined as PW.2, through him OPD book and X-ray are marked under Ex.P.12 & 13.
According to the evidence of this witness the petitioner sustained undisplaced fracture of left calcaneus.
He was treated conservatively.
He examined the petitioner for assessment of disability.
Petitioner suffered disability of left lower limb at 12% and whole body disability at 6%.
This aspect is not impeached during the course of cross-examination.
According to the petitioner he was working as coolie and he was earning Rs.25,000/- p.m.
But no documents are produced by the petitioner to show his exact income.
As per Ex.P10- discharge summary and Ex.P7 wound certificate and as per the injuries mentioned at point No.1 & 2 of wound certificate, the injuries sustained by the petitioner are grievous in nature.
No other evidence is placed by the respondents to disbelieve the evidence of the doctor in this regard.
By considering the same this court is of the opinion that the disability would be 6% in this case by considering the age and avocation of the petitioner.
As per the Aadhar card marked at Ex.P8, as per this document the year of birth of the petitioner is mentioned as 1948.
The accident was occurred in the year-2022.
So, as on the date of the accident the petitioner was aged 74 years.
As per Sarala Verma's case, the proper multiplier applicable to the age of petitioner is '5'.
Hence, I inclined to award future loss of income at Rs.15,500/- X 12 X 5 X 6% =Rs.55,800/- which is the total loss of future income.
e) FOOD, NOURISHMENT AND CONVEYANCE ; As per Ex.P10 discharge summary, the petitioner took treatment as inpatient for a period of 4 days.
As per the wound certificate marked at Ex.P7 the injuries sustained by the petitioner are grievous in nature.
If we perused the evidence of the doctor certainly the injuries mentioned in the wound certificate is causing a considerable disability to the petitioner.

By considering the nature of the injuries and period he spent to overcome the pain and other allied effects of the accident Hence looking to the treatment taken by the petitioner and injuries sustained he is entitled for compensation of Rs.25,000/- towards food and nourishment,
conveyance.
f) ATTENDANT CHARGES:
The petitioner sustained grievous injuries in the accident.
The petitioner was admitted as inpatient for 4 days in the hospital and there is no evidence or pleading in this regard to show that the petitioner is in need of attendant.

But by considering the nature of the grievous injuries as discussed above, one month of healing period including the inpatient period may be considered to award attendant charges at Rs.1,000/- per day i.e., Rs.4,000/- in total.

Chunchegowda vs N.E.K.S.R.T.C on 10 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/178061914/
6
g) Towards loss of amenities and enjoyment of life:
The petitioner admitted to the hospital for the injuries sustained by him, which might certainly have deprived him of the basic comforts and enjoyment.
Therefore, it is just and proper to award a reasonable sum of Rs.20,000/- under this head.
h) Towards future medical expenses: The evidence of doctor is silent about future medical expenses.
Thus, in the absence of evidence, the petitioner is not entitle for compensation under this head.

Thus, the petitioner is entitled for compensation under the following heads:
a) Towards pain and agony Rs. 25,000/-
b) Towards medical expenses Rs. 24,000/-
c) Towards loss of income Rs. 31,000/-
d) Towards disability Rs. 55,800/-
e) Towards food, nourishment  and conveyance Rs. 25,000/-
f) Towards attendant charges Rs. 4,000/-
g) Towards loss of amenities Rs. 20,000/-
 _______________
. Liability:-
According to the petitioner the respondent No.1 is the owner and there is a internal insurance to the offending vehicle.

Hence, the respondent No.1 is liable to pay compensation to the petitioner with interest at the rate of 6% p.a., Accordingly,
I answer this issue partly in the affirmative.

ISSUE NO.3:
20.

For the foregoing reasons, I proceed to pass the following:
O RDE R
The petition filed by the petitioner U/s 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act is hereby partly allowed with cost.
Chunchegowda vs N.E.K.S.R.T.C on 10 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/178061914/

7 The petitioner is entitled for total compensation amount of Rs.1,84,800/- (Rupees One lakh eighty four thousand eight hundred only) with interest at the rate of 6% p.a., from the date of petition till the realization from respondent.
The respondent No.1 is directed to deposit the compensation amount within 60 days from the date of this order.
Considering the quantum of amount awarded to petitioner, it is ordered to release entire amount in his favour.
Advocate fee is fixed at 1,500/-.
Draw up award accordingly.
(Dictated to the Stenographer directly on the computer, corrected by me and then pronounced in the open court on this the 10th day of June, 2024)
(Kanchi Mayanna Goutam)
